class_name: 放置-非実現-ナイデシマウ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

patterns.usage_note: Reports that an action ended up never happening, carrying the regret that しまう typically adds in this construction — elsewhere しまう can mark bare completion with no regret at all; unlike ないでおく (1481) nothing was intended, and unlike ないでいる (1471) the window has closed. In contemporary Japanese the frozen noun 〜ずじまい, built from the same ず + しまい, is far commoner than the finite verb, and 〜ないままになる is the neutral alternative. Be aware that 〜ずにしまう is easily read as the lexical 仕舞う "put away" (使わずにしまった), so the context has to force the aspectual reading.

examples.ruby: せっかくの休[やす]みなのに、どこにも出[で]かけないでしまった。
examples.english: I finally had time off, and ended up going nowhere at all.

examples.ruby: 借[か]りた本[ほん]を、とうとう読[よ]まないでしまった。
examples.english: In the end I never got around to reading the book I'd borrowed.

examples.ruby: 同僚[どうりょう]には結局[けっきょく]相談[そうだん]しないでしまった。
examples.english: In the end I never did bring it up with my colleague.
